## Teaching Approach

My goal in teaching Industrial and Systems Engineering is to help students connect mathematical and computational models to the decisions they inform. I emphasize problem formulation, explicit assumptions, computational implementation, and interpretation of results.

At the University at Buffalo, I have led recitations, laboratory sessions, lectures, and review sessions in undergraduate and graduate courses.


## Selected Teaching Experience

::: {.teaching-block}

### Probability, Statistics & Simulation

**EAS 305 — Applied Probability & Statistics**

Led recitations, designed recitation materials, delivered Minitab laboratory instruction, and conducted exam-review lectures.

**IE 477 — Simulation Modeling and Analysis**

Led recitations and course lectures and designed instructional materials using Arena and @RISK.

**IE 551 — Simulation and Stochastic Models**

Delivered course instruction and supported students through group-specific active office hours.

:::


::: {.teaching-block}

### Manufacturing & Operations

**IE 406/506 — Computer Integrated Manufacturing**

Led laboratory tutorials using Autodesk Fusion 360 for 3D CAD modeling and manufacturing.

**IE 505 — Production Planning and Control**

Supported instruction in core production-planning and operations topics.

:::


::: {.teaching-block}

### Health Systems

**IE 585 — Industrial Engineering Principles and Practice in Healthcare**

Guest lectured on PICO question formulation and the analysis of complex observational healthcare datasets for interpretable decision support.

:::

## Teaching Development

In Spring 2025, I contributed to *Effective Pedagogy for Teaching Assistants* at the University at Buffalo, sharing approaches for leading recitations and addressing teaching-assistant challenges using Universal Design for Learning.
